articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos España vs República Checa
articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a España y República Checa en el Carlos Tartiere, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la UEFA Nations League 2026-27
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a España y República Checa en el Carlos Tartiere, correspondiente a la tercera jornada de la UEFA Nations League 2026-27
articles.body: España recibe a la República Checa este sábado en Oviedo, en la tercera jornada del Grupo A3. La campeona del mundo llega lanzada. Ganó 3-2 a Inglaterra en Wembley y goleó 4-1 a Croacia en Sevilla, con doblete de Lamine Yamal, por lo que lidera el grupo con puntuación perfecta. La selección de Santi Denia, en cambio, suma dos derrotas. Cayó 2-1 ante Croacia y 2-0 ante Inglaterra en Praga, un partido en el que jugó más de una hora con diez por la expulsión de Pavel Šulc. Favorito para el partido entre España vs República Checa Las casas de apuestas no tienen dudas. Codere paga la victoria de España a cuota 1.06, por 9.5 del empate y 35.00 del triunfo checo. Los precedentes refuerzan la lectura: España no ha perdido nunca contra la República Checa desde la separación de Checoslovaquia (cinco victorias y dos empates) y ha ganado los cuatro partidos que ha jugado como local ante este rival. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan ofrece algo más de valor que el del ganador. España es una máquina ofensiva, pero no ha dejado su portería a cero en esta Nations League. Encajó dos goles en Wembley y uno de Beljo ante Croacia. La República Checa, por su parte, marcó en su estreno ante Croacia y mantiene su amenaza a balón parado, un recurso que puede castigar a una defensa española que está probando piezas. Sin embargo, los checos llegan sin Schick ni Souček y se quedaron en blanco ante Inglaterra, así que la balanza no está clara. En las apuestas deportivas, Codere paga el sí a 2.75 y el no a 1.4. Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta a un partido con ventaja española, pero con un tope razonable. España ha anotado cuatro y tres goles en sus dos partidos, aunque los dos han tenido cinco goles en total por los tantos encajados. La República Checa, por el contrario, se mueve en marcadores cortos: dos goles en sus dos encuentros contando los dos partidos (uno marcado y cuatro encajados, con diez hombres en el último). Con un rival que sabe defenderse y tiene que competir por un resultado digno, lo lógico es un partido de pocos goles para el rival. Codere paga el más de 3.5 goles a 1.8 y el menos de 3.5 a 1.95. Equipo con más córners El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante, y aquí la clave es quién tendrá el balón. España domina las posesiones largas y, ante Croacia, ya había botado seis saques de esquina en el tramo final del partido, uno de los cuales acabó en el gol de Pubill. La República Checa, sin Souček, se ha mostrado muy replegada: ante Inglaterra tuvo un 33.8 % de posesión y apenas seis disparos, con 22 de su rival. Si Denia plantea de nuevo una línea baja, España acumulará llegadas y córners. El pronóstico es que España será el equipo con más córners a 1.13, por 7.5 del caso contrario.

articles.title: Dodgers Reportedly Make Decision On Starting Pitcher For NLDS Game 1
articles.summary: Tarik Skubal will reportedly get the nod in Saturday's contest at Dodgers Stadium.
articles.body: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has a plethora of options on who he wants on the mound for Game 1 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves.But it appears that Tarik Skubal will get the nod in Saturday's contest at Dodgers Stadium. The left-handed ace was the Dodgers' biggest midseason acquisition when the two-time Cy Young winner joined the two-time defending World Series champions from Detroit in a blockbuster trade. He initially struggled in his first few starts but got back into the form that made him one of baseball's most feared pitchers. Skubal finished the regular season 3-2 with a 2.52 ERA in eight starts for the Dodgers. The team will want to lean on Skubal as much as they can in the postseason, especially as he is expected to one of the biggest free agents this winter. His start could then allow Yoshinobu Yamamoto or Blake Snell to start for the Dodgers for Game 2. The Dodgers (93-60) are in the postseason for the 14th consecutive season, tying the Braves’ record from 1991-2005. As for the Braves, it remains to be seen who skipper Walt Weiss will go with. Presumably it would be Chris Sale, but the staff ace pitched in both Game 2 and Game 3 of the wild-card series against the Phillies.

articles.title: Braves vs. Dodgers Meet In The Postseason Again: NL Foes' MLB Playoff History
articles.summary: The Dodgers and Braves will face off in the playoffs for the sixth time and the fifth time since 2010. Here's the history.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Dodgers and Atlanta Braves have a couple of things in common over the last 30 years. One commonality is star first baseman Freddie Freeman, who has played for and won a World Series with both the Dodgers and Braves. Meanwhile, a recurring theme is the two teams being good at the same time and meeting in the postseason. On that note, the Braves and Dodgers will face off in the 2026 National League Division Series starting with Game 1 on Saturday, with Los Angeles having home-field advantage in the series. This will be the sixth playoff matchup between the two franchises, with four of the five finished series coming since the decade of the 2010s. Here's how the Braves and Dodgers' five playoff series have fared: Braves Crush Dodgers In '96 Coming off winning the 1995 World Series, the Braves were a well-oiled machine in 1996, and the Dodgers were just an object in their way. While Los Angeles held Atlanta to just 10 runs in the 1996 NLDS, the Braves held the Dodgers to half that amount in what was a three-game sweep. John Smoltz surrendered just one run and six baserunners (four hits and two walks) over nine innings pitched for the Braves in Game 1, which required extra innings. Then, catcher Javy López led off the top of the 10th inning with a home run off Antonio Osuna, proving to be enough for the 2-1 victory. Greg Maddux followed with seven potent innings for Atlanta in Game 2, giving up no walks or earned runs through seven innings. However, the Braves would need to flip the script in the later innings, and a pair of solo home runs in the top of the seventh from star first baseman Fred McGriff and right fielder Jermaine Dye did just that, as Atlanta would win, 3-2. The Braves closed out the series on their home field, with left-hander Tom Glavine surrendering just one run over 6 ⅓ innings in a 5-2 victory. As for their work with the bats, McGriff brought home a run on a double in the bottom of the first and Atlanta had a four-run fourth inning that saw second baseman Mark Lemke hit a two-run double and third baseman and burgeoning superstar Chipper Jones hit a two-run home run. Atlanta went on to win the NL pennant for a second consecutive year. Granted, the Braves blew a 2-0 series lead to the New York Yankees in the World Series. Dodgers Silence Braves In '13 The 2013 MLB season marked the Braves' first NL East title in eight years, but the vibes at Turner Field were muted by the Dodgers in Game 1 of the NLDS. A pair of two-run innings in the second and third, highlighted by a two-run home run from first baseman Adrián González, and a fourth-inning RBI single from veteran second baseman Mark Ellis ultimately put the game out of reach for the Braves. Los Angeles scored a sixth run on a sixth-inning double from Hanley Ramírez in a 6-1 win, while superstar southpaw Clayton Kershaw carved up Atlanta's offense with 12 strikeouts over seven innings. Atlanta bounced back in Game 2, getting a 4-3 victory that saw it fend off a late Los Angeles push which saw Ramírez hit a two-run home run to pull the Dodgers within one run in the eighth inning. Braves left-hander Mike Minor continued to evade damage, surrendering just one run over 6 ⅓ innings, while outfielder Jason Heyward provided needed separation for Atlanta with a two-run single in the bottom of the seventh. The Braves got out to a 2-0 lead in the opening frame of Game 3, but the Dodgers would rock right-hander Julio Teherán out of the game after 2 ⅔ innings and proceed to rake the rest of the way. As part of a 13-6 win that saw the Dodgers tally 14 hits, left fielder Carl Crawford and third baseman Juan Uribe each homered, with Ramírez and rookie sensation Yasiel Puig logging three hits apiece. Then, Atlanta looked on track to force a Game 5, as it held a 3-2 lead in the bottom of the eighth inning in Game 4. But Uribe sent Dodger Stadium into a state of delirium with a go-ahead and ultimate game and series-winning, two-run home run. Kenley Jansen struck out the side in the top of the ninth. Moreover, Crawford hit a pair of solo home runs earlier in the game (bottom of the first and third). Dodgers Silence Them Again In '18 It was eerily similar to 2013. This time around, the Braves hadn't posted a winning record or made the playoffs since that 2013 series against the Dodgers and had a presumably bright future ensuing around a blossoming young core that included Freeman, outfielder Ronald Acuña Jr. and second baseman Ozzie Albies, among others. But the 2018 NLDS went sour quickly for the Braves. Atlanta failed to score in each of the first two games of the series and was held to a combined nine hits, losing 6-0 in Game 1 and 3-0 in Game 2. Left-hander Hyun Jin Ryu went seven innings for the Dodgers in Game 1, with the bulk of the scoring coming off a three-run home run from first baseman Max Muncy, with left fielder Joc Pederson and second baseman Kike Hernández each hitting solo home runs. Regarding Game 2, the Braves ran into Kershaw, who threw eight scoreless innings and gave up just two baserunners (two hits), while the Dodgers' three runs came on a two-run home run from Manny Machado (it was a moment in time) and a solo homer from catcher Yasmani Grandal. Atlanta's offense finally came to life in Game 3, as it got five runs in the bottom of the second off Walker Buehler, a frame highlighted by a grand slam from Acuña. Now, the Dodgers managed to level the score at 5-all with a two-run single from third baseman Justin Turner in the top of the third, a two-run home run from left fielder Chris Taylor in the fifth and a solo homer from Muncy later in the inning. But Freeman would bail out the Braves with a solo homer in the bottom of the sixth, and they held on to win, 6-5. With that said, the Dodgers closed out the series in Game 4. After trailing 2-1 through five innings, Los Angeles would plate two runs in the sixth on a pinch-hit single from David Freese and three more in the seventh on a three-run homer from Machado, going on to win 6-2. The effort also included 4 ⅔ shutout innings from the Dodgers' bullpen. Los Angeles would go on to win the NL pennant for a second consecutive year but also lose in the World Series for a second consecutive year. Dodgers Roar Back In '20 This series was, undoubtedly, the most painful of this bunch for the Atlanta faithful. This series took place at Globe Life Field, home of the Texas Rangers. All playoff series beyond the wild-card round in 2020 took place at a neutral site in what was just a 60-game regular season due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Game 1 of the 2020 NL Championship Series was a pitchers' duel through eight innings until the Braves struck for four runs in the top of the ninth, highlighted by a two-run home run from Albies and a solo blast from third baseman Austin Riley. Atlanta took control of the series with an 8-7 win in Game 2 to take a 2-0 series lead. In said victory, the Braves got home runs from Freeman and Albies, who had a game-high three hits. The Dodgers got off the mat in a big way in Game 3, though, essentially ending the game in the opening frame with an 11-run first inning and four more runs over the next two innings, culminating in a 15-3 win. In the aforementioned first-inning shellacking, the Dodgers got a grand slam from Muncy, a three-run home run from Pederson — who had a game-high four hits — and a solo homer from Edwin Ríos. All that said, the Braves thumped the Dodgers in Game 4, 10-2, to put Los Angeles on the ropes. Most of the damage came in a six-run sixth inning, which broke a 1-1 tie. Designated hitter Marcell Ozuna had a game-high four hits for the Braves, highlighted by a solo home run in the seventh and an RBI double in the sixth; the Dodgers had three hits. But then it happened. Trailing 2-1 in the top of the sixth in Game 5, the Dodgers ripped off a pair of three-run innings to get a 7-3 victory and keep their season alive. Their seven total runs came on a fourth-inning solo home run from shortstop Corey Seager, a three-run homer from catcher Will Smith in the sixth, another homer from Seager in the seventh (it was a two-run shot this time) and an RBI single from Mookie Betts. Then, the Dodgers got all the runs they'd need in the opening inning of Game 6, as Seager and Turner each hit solo home runs and center fielder Cody Bellinger hit an RBI single in a 3-1 win for Los Angeles, which got six scoreless innings from Buehler. Game 7 was back and forth, as the Braves scored a run in the first and second innings, with the Dodgers getting those two runs back in the bottom of the third and Atlanta taking back the lead in the top of the fourth. But solo home runs from Hernández in the sixth and Bellinger in the seventh would be enough for the Dodgers to get the win and pull off the series comeback. After coming back down 3-1 in the NLCS, the Dodgers went on to beat the Tampa Bay Rays in the 2020 World Series, marking the franchise's first championship since 1988. Braves Get Dodgers Back In '21 The Dodgers and Braves ran it back in the 2021 NLCS, and Atlanta exacted its revenge. Game 1 was a low-scoring affair that saw the Dodgers deploy a bullpen game, while the Braves got six plausible innings from left-hander Max Fried. The game entered the ninth inning tied at 2-all, but Riley — who hit a solo home run in the bottom of the fourth — ensured there would be no extra innings with a walk-off, RBI single. Los Angeles began Game 2 with a bang, as Seager hit a two-run home run in the top of the first, but Joc Pederson (yes, he left the Dodgers after the 2020 season and was traded to the Braves during the 2021 season) would match the long ball with a two-run homer of his own in the bottom of the fourth. Like in Game 1, Game 2 was tied entering the ninth inning, and, yes, the Braves walked it off again. This time, the walk-off hit came on an infield single from left fielder Eddie Rosario, who finished with a game-high four hits in a 5-4 win. Atlanta looked poised to take a 3-0 series lead in Game 3, as it led 5-2 entering the bottom of the eighth. But a three-run home run from Bellinger in the bottom of the eighth and an RBI double from Betts later in the inning would give the Dodgers a desperately needed 6-5 win. That said, the Braves put the Dodgers on the brink of elimination with a 9-2 victory in Game 4 that saw Rosario hit two home runs and log a second four-hit game in the series. Freeman and outfielder Adam Duvall also homered for Atlanta. At first, Atlanta looked like it was going to roll to a Game 5 victory, as Freeman launched a two-run home run in the top of the first. But the Los Angeles bats came to life in momentous fashion, as the Dodgers plated 11 runs to fend off elimination. The star of the show was Dodgers third baseman Chris Taylor, who cranked three home runs, while left fielder AJ Pollock blasted two long balls. At this point in time, the winner of each game was identical to the 2020 NLCS, bringing back nightmare memories for Braves fans. But Game 6 had a much different finish. Riley drew first blood for the Braves with an RBI double in the bottom of the first, and a three-home run from Rosario (yeah, he had a good series) in the fourth would put Atlanta up to stay, with it going on to win the game, 4-2. Moreover, the Braves would beat the Houston Astros in the World Series, marking the franchise's first championship triumph since 1995. By the way, this all came with Acuña missing the second half of the season and the entire postseason due to a knee injury. Act 6 of this playoff rivalry commences on Saturday night at 4 p.m. ET on FOX.

articles.title: Will Aaron Judge Be Available For Yankees' ALDS Series vs. Rays?
articles.summary: Will Aaron Judge be available for Game 1 for Yankees vs. Rays on Saturday? Here's the latest on the Yankees star.
articles.body: The New York Yankees surged its way to the American League Division Series after its two-game sweep over the Boston Red Sox. And yet, the Yankees' dominant series win came without star Aaron Judge. Judge has been out with a calf strain injury since Sept. 19, when the Yankees originally moved him to the 10-day injured list. Especially as the Yankees creep towards its next postseason series against the Tampa Bay Rays, Judge's timeline and likeliness of making the 26-man roster this weekend is still unknown. The Yankees have until Saturday morning to submit their final rosters ahead of Game 1 at 6:30 p.m. in St. Petersburg, Florida. If Judge were to be added to the roster, it would be his first roster appearance this postseason run for New York. Manager Aaron Boone provided clarity on Judge ahead of submitting the roster, and gave a status update on Judge’s health. "The trainers will obviously play a big part in this. As the day unfolds, we'll see where we're at and what it potentially looks like for the series," Boone said. Although Judge has been a part of live batting practice, Boone is still weighing in how, and when, Judge can be utilized against the Rays. "It's just as far as him and the field, potentially," Boone said. "But we're looking at the days and so it's more, 'Is he going to be available at some point in this series, potentially, as a player?' That's what we're kind of weighing and then seeing where he's at now these last few days having taken live [batting practice]." The Yankees' postseason run continues tomorrow at 6:30 p.m. in a three-game divisional series against the Rays. articles.title: Texas Tech QB Thomas Castellanos Among NCAA Athletes Ruled Ineligible
articles.summary: Court rulings in Kentucky and Ohio reversed the eligibility for multiple NCAA athletes, including Texas Tech QB Thomas Castellanos.
articles.body: A summer of NCAA football and basketball players gaining a fifth year of eligibility has given way to a fall of seeing those decisions reversed. On Friday, court rulings in Ohio and Kentucky left multiple players without eligibility for the 2026-27 season — at least for now. One player reportedly impacted by the outcome in Kentucky is Texas Tech quarterback Thomas Castellanos. The 12th-ranked Red Raiders ruled Castellanos out for Saturday's game against Colorado (7:30 p.m. ET on FOX). Castellanos had been serving as the backup to starting quarterback Will Hammond throughout Texas Tech's 4-0 start to the season. He transferred to Lubbock, Texas, from Florida State after receiving a temporary restraining order on July 31st. The Red Raiders acquired Castellanos after the NCAA ruled former quarterback Brendan Sorsby ineligible for the 2026 season following a gambling scandal. Texas Tech is trying to return to the College Football Playoff, and defend its Big 12 title. Several college basketball programs were also impacted by Friday's court rulings. A ruling in Ohio deemed Cincinnati's MJ Collins ineligible, while the ruling in Kentucky deemed Mark Mitchell (Missouri), Seth Trimble (Louisville) and Skyy Clark (LSU) ineligible, among others. Collins followed coach Jerrod Calhoun from Utah State to Cincinnati after finishing fourth among all Mountain West players in scoring last season (17.5 points per game). Mitchell returned to Missouri, Trimble transferred to Louisville after four seasons at ACC rival North Carolina and Clark was hoping to play at a fourth school in five seasons. It's important to note, each of these decisions remains temporary.

articles.title: Neeraj Chauhan clinches recurve bronze, defeats Dhiraj Bommadevara in all-India clash at Asian Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Indian archer Neeraj Chauhan won the bronze medal in the men's recurve individual event at the Asian Games 2026 after defeating compatriot
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian archer Neeraj Chauhan won the bronze medal in the men's recurve individual event at the Asian Games 2026 after defeating compatriot Dhiraj Bommadevara 6-4 at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Multipurpose Square on Saturday.In an all-Indian medal contest, Chauhan held his nerve to finish ahead of Bommadevara and claim the bronze medal.Chauhan started strongly and won the first game 29-26.Bommadevara hit 7, 9 and 10 for a total of 26, while Chauhan shot 10, 9 and 10 to score 29.Bommadevara hit back in the second set. He scored 28, including a 10 and an X, while Chauhan managed 27. Bommadevara won the set 2-0 to level the match at 2-2.The third set went Chauhan's way. He scored 28 with an X, 9 and 9, while Bommadevara scored 29 with an X, 9 and 10.Bommadevara won the set 2-0, moving ahead 4-2.Chauhan then responded in the fourth set. He produced 30, hitting 10, X and 10, while Bommadevara scored 28. Chauhan took the set 2-0, bringing the match level at 4-4.The fifth and final set decided the bronze medal.Chauhan delivered when it mattered most, shooting 29 with an X, 9 and another X. articles.body: India’s medal-winning campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 has reached 80 medals, with the contingent winning 18 gold, 26 silver and 36 bronze medals. India are currently fifth in the overall medal standings.India’s medal tally received a major boost over the last two days, with the contingent adding gold medals across boxing, wrestling, archery, hockey and golf. Lovlina Borgohain, Parveen Hooda, Ankush Panghal, Sujeet Kalkal, the Indian women’s hockey team, Kumkum Mohod and Pranavi Urs have all contributed gold medals to India’s latest surge.Kumkum also won silver alongside Dhiraj Bommadevara in the mixed recurve team event, while India’s women’s golf team of Pranavi Urs, Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar secured silver.On October 3, Kumkum Mohod added another gold by winning the women’s individual recurve event. However, Han responded with a strong counterattack and scored six points in quick succession to take a 7-6 lead.Aman then turned the bout around with an important move that earned him four points. articles.title: Friendly defeat in the international break
articles.summary: 2-1 loss to FC Blau-Weiß LinzAs part of the opening of a new sports facility in Pischelsdorf, our Red Bulls played a friendly match there against FC Blau-Wei...
articles.body:
As part of the opening of a new sports facility in Pischelsdorf, our Red Bulls played a friendly match there against FC Blau-Weiß Linz. The clash with the 2. Liga leaders ended in a narrow 1–2 defeat.

Early on, Edmund Baidoo headed our boys into the lead following a fine assist by Konate. The Ghanaian also hit the crossbar shortly afterwards, while Dominik Schmid and Stefan Lainer failed to convert good chances. Linz captain Manuel Maranda equalized with a header just before the break. Shortly after the restart, the Linz side turned the match around, scoring in the 47th minute to seal a 2–1 win.

We wrapped up a good week of training with a genuinely good friendly match, even if the final result wasn't what we wanted. That's a bit frustrating. However, we were able to implement much of what we had planned and handled many situations well, especially in possession. We also created enough chances to win the game. Now we have two days off before we can fully prepare for the next block of important matches.

The following 10 international players were unavailable today: Abubakr Barry, Kevin Boma, Aboubacar Camara, Filip Matijasevic, Bartosz Mazurek, John Mellberg, Leandro Morgalla, Nikola Sarcevic, Haris Tabakovic and Valentin Zabransky.

Missing due to injury were Enrique Aguilar (thigh), Soumaila Diabate (thigh), Johannes Moser (adductor), Justin Omoregie (ankle), Damir Redzic (ankle), Nikolas Veratschnig (knee) and Christian Zawieschitzky (adductor).

On the positive side, Gaoussou Diakite returned to action after a long injury lay-off.

FC Liefering youngsters Filip Aleksic, Teo Hupfauf, Julian Hussauf, Ilia Ivanschitz, Riquelme, Lassina Traore and Jakob Zangerl were also included in the squad for the friendly match.

The team has the weekend off from training before preparations begin on Monday for the upcoming ADMIRAL Bundesliga match against GAK.

articles.title: Bayern Munich formulating goalkeeper plan for 2026/27
articles.summary: FC Bayern has a strategy for the goalkeeper position.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich is beginning to plan for a major change in its goalkeeping department, with Manuel Neuer and Sven Ulreich both potentially heading toward retirement at the end of the season.

According to Kicker's Frank Linkesch (via @iMiaSanMia ), Bayern Munich plans to hold talks with both goalkeepers about their futures during either the November international break or the winter break. The current expectation is that both Neuer and Ulreich will retire when the season concludes.

If that happens, Jonas Urbig is expected to take over as Bayern Munich's clear No. 1 next season. The club is already looking at options for a goalkeeper to serve as Urbig's backup.

Bayern Munich has established a specific profile for the position: the new No. 2 should be experienced, comfortable accepting a backup role, relatively inexpensive to sign, and capable of contributing with his feet. That last requirement is particularly important under Vincent Kompany, who expects his goalkeepers to be comfortable in possession, even during training.

No goalkeeper has been approached at this stage, but FC Augsburg's Finn Dahmen, Fulham's Bernd Leno, and Hoffenheim's Oliver Baumann are among the names being discussed internally. While Leno and Baumann are older veterans, Dahmen is still just 28 years old and may be more inclined to remain a No. 1 goalkeeper with FC Augsburg.

Bayern Munich is also taking its time with the No. 3 position, which could ultimately be filled by an academy goalkeeper or an external signee.

articles.title: Dylan Larkin Being Booed by Red Wings Fans Amid Trade Request Addressed by HC, 'I Feel Bad For Him'
articles.summary: Detroit Red Wings coach Todd McClellan said he felt sympathy for Dylan Larkin after the former captain was met with vitriol from his home crowd during Friday night's season-opening shutout loss to the New York Rangers.
articles.body:
Detroit Red Wings coach Todd McClellan said he felt sympathy for Dylan Larkin after the former captain was met with vitriol from his home crowd during Friday night's season-opening shutout loss to the New York Rangers.

Larkin, who was stripped of his captaincy after requesting a trade this offseason and placed on IR ahead of Friday's puck drop, received a chorus of boos when introduced alongside his scratched teammates at Little Caesars Arena.

McLellan pushed back after the game against TNT studio analyst's Paul Bissonnette concluding on the broadcast the Wings were trying to embarrass Larkin with the announcement.

"Dylan, today, being a part of the team, he wanted to be out there for the ceremony... Dylan's explanation was, 'I don't want the rest of my teammates, the ones that aren't dressed, to not be out there,'" McLellan said after the Red Wings' 2-0 loss. "So, we went out as a team."

McLellan continued, "Obviously, he's got to live with the ramifications of asking for a trade. It's not comfortable for anybody. I feel bad for him, I do."

Larkin's trade request wasn't the only point of contention from Red Wings fans, which were already leading chants against the team's ownership while down by one goal early in Friday's loss.

The Red Wings have yet to name a permanent replacement for former general manager Steve Yzerman, who was fired in the wake of Larkin's trade request and whose departure has been followed by notable roster issues in Detroit.

These include allowing Patrick Kane to sign with the Chicago Blackhawks in free agency despite past negotiations with Yzerman, missing the deadline to extend winger Alex DeBrincat's expiring contract for eight years and watching restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson leave for Sweden after starting the season without a contract.

"Everyone has a right to express their feelings, and we've just got to deal with it," Red Wings defenseman Moritz Seider said after the game (h/t WXYZ Detroit's Alex Crescenti ). "I thought we handled it pretty well."

Larkin, who is signed through the 2030-31 season with a full no-trade clause through the 2027-28 campaign, has reportedly given the Red Wings a limited list of teams he would be willing to accept a move to.

The Detroit Free Press ' Helene St. James initially reported that list including the Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights and Florida Panthers.

Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Friday Larkin has since expanded his list to "around eight" teams including the Colorado Avalanche, Washington Capitals, Dallas Stars and Tampa Bay Lightning.

Detroit fans will hope either interim general manager Shawn Horcoff, or who the team eventually tabs as a permanent replacement to Yzerman, is able to either resolve the standoff with Larkin or find a palatable deal that will allow the Red Wings to replace their top-line center despite their current lack of negotiating leverage.

articles.title: Récord de velocidad en Francia: cazan al conductor de un Porsche 911 GT3 a 312 km/h y por la noche
articles.standfirst: El anterior registro en el país vecino databa del año pasado... a 286 km/h
articles.summary: El anterior registro en el país vecino databa del año pasado... a 286 km/h
articles.body: La Gendarmería francesa acaba de registrar un nuevo récord de velocidad en sus carreteras después de cazar a un conductor suizo de 48 años… ¡¡a 312 km/h y por la noche!! Sucedió hace unos días en la A40, en la región de la Alta Saboya, cuando un Porsche 911 GT3 de la generación 991 fue controlado por un radar a esa velocidad, en una carretera en la que el límite máximo era de 130 km/h. Es decir, circulaba nada menos que 182 km/h por encima de lo que permite la Ley, es decir, a más del doble de la velocidad de la vía... y prácticamente al máximo de lo que permite el vehículo, que homologa 320 km/h de punta. El conductor del Porsche fue inmediatamente detenido por la Gendarmerie, su licencia de conducir fue revocada y el vehículo confiscado. Sólo cuando abonó una fianza de 1.500 euros se le permitió salir en libertad. Pero su aventura no quedará ahí porque ahora tendrá que afrontar lo peor de las consecuencias de su acción: un proceso penal. Su carta de presentación ante la justicia francesa no le favorecerá mucho ya que se trata del récord absoluto de velocidad registrado… y con diferencia. El anterior registro estaba en poder del conductor de un Audi RS 3 que fue controlado a más de 285 km/h el año pasado. Según medios franceses, el juicio se celebrará el año próximo y puede haber incluso penas de prisión para el infractor (tres meses, según la legislación gala). Este tipo de delitos, como sucede en España, tienen carácter penal, de ahí que la pena de cárcel esté sobre la mesa… como también una súper multa de más de 4.000 euros. Con todo… el dueño del Porsche tuvo suerte de no haber sido detenido en su país de origen, donde las multas se imponen en función de la capacidad económica del infractor. De momento, no podrá conducir durante una temporada en Francia… pero no se descarta que las autoridades suizas puedan intervenir de oficio al tratarse de un caso excepcional y ampliar la prohibición también a su territorio. Se da la circunstancia de que la Gendarmerie francesa, como también sucede en EE.UU., es proclive a publicar este tipo de situaciones para que sirvan como ejemplarizantes para los conductores. De hecho, y sin ir más lejos, hoy mismo ha publicado otra situación parecida en la que un conductor de un Audi RS Q3 ha sido interceptado a 239 km/h en la A9, una carretera con límite de 110 km/h.

articles.title: South Africa’s Pretorius smashes Gayle’s T20 cricket record score
articles.summary: South African Lhuan-dre Pretorius hit 50 in 24 balls, needed 16 more to reach 100 and took another 18 to hit 150.
articles.body:
Lhuan-dre Pretorius hit 188 not out off 79 deliveries in Bloemfontein to break Chris Gayle’s record score in the T20 format.

Playing for the Titans against the Knights in the South African CSA Challenge, the 20-year-old left-hander opened the batting and hit 13 sixes and 14 fours in his innings to surpass Gayle’s 175 for Bengaluru in the Indian Premier League in 2013.

Pretorius reached 50 in 24 balls, needed 16 more to get to his century and took another 18 to hit 150.

Gayle scored his 175 off 66 balls, striking 17 sixes and 13 fours.

The 20-year-old has represented South Africa in all three international formats. He was making his first Titans appearance of the season after scoring 226 total runs, tied for most with Dewald Brevis, in a three-nation series in Namibia in September.

On Friday, he dominated the strike, facing the equivalent of more than 13 overs to tie Australians Aaron Finch and Marcus Stoinis for the most balls faced in a T20 innings.

The second-highest scorer was Sinethemba Qeshile with 14 as the Titans finished on 267-3.

They then bowled out the Knights for 143 to win by 124 runs.

The Titans total was the second-highest in the competition’s history, behind their 271 also against the Kings in 2022. In that match, Brevis hit 162, until Friday, a competition record. This time he made seven.

The Cricinfo website calculated that in 91 T20 games, Pretorius has a strike rate of 150.44.

articles.body: India produced one of their biggest medal hauls of the Asian Games on Saturday, with gold medals coming in men's hockey, T20 cricket, wrestling, golf and archery.The men's hockey team capped the day by beating Malaysia 5-1 in the final to retain their Asian Games title and book a place at the 2028 Olympics.India's medal tally now stands at 85 medals - 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.Hockey delivers another golden momentCaptain Harmanpreet Singh led from the front with two goals as India beat Malaysia 5-1 to win the men's hockey gold.Harmanpreet scored in the 11th and 57th minutes, while Jugraj Singh, Hardik Singh and Shilanand Lakra also found the net. Malaysia's only goal came from Shello Silverius in the 14th minute.Harmanpreet finished as the tournament's top scorer with 12 goals. India also earned 14 penalty corners compared to Malaysia's two.The victory gave India their fifth Asian Games men's hockey gold, after previous triumphs in 1966, 1998, 2014 and 2022. India also became only the second country after Pakistan to win back-to-back Asian Games men's hockey golds.Harmanpreet became the first Indian men's hockey captain to lead the team to two Asian Games gold medals.The triumph came a day after the women's team beat defending champions China 1-0 to win their first Asian Games gold in 44 years and secure an Olympic berth.It was the first time that both Indian hockey teams finished on top of the podium at the same Asian Games.Aman wins wrestling gold, Antim settles for silverAman Sehrawat upgraded his bronze from the 2023 Hangzhou Games to gold by beating North Korea's reigning world champion Chong Song Han 10-7 in the men's 57kg final.The 23-year-old was initially frustrated by Han's defensive approach but took control after being put on the clock. attack.Deepak Punia added a bronze in the men's 97kg category after beating Mongolia's Gankhuyang Ganbataar 2-1.India finished the wrestling competition with six medals — two gold, two silver and two bronze.Abhishek, Tilak power India to cricket goldIndia retained their Asian Games men's T20 cricket title after beating Pakistan by 19 runs in the final.Abhishek Sharma smashed 61 off 28 balls, hitting seven sixes, while Tilak Varma produced an unbeaten 51 off 22 balls as India posted 211/6.Pakistan fought back through Hasan Nawaz, who scored 96 off 51 balls, but India held their nerve to restrict them to 192/6.The victory also extended India's head-to-head dominance over Pakistan to 6-0 since the start of the 2024 T20 World Cup.Pranavi makes history in golfPranavi Urs became the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games golf gold.The 23-year-old held her nerve despite a triple bogey on the third hole and recovered with three birdies to finish the final round at even-par 70.She finished at 15-under 265, one stroke ahead of China's Yin Ruoning.Pranavi's gold also helped India win the women's team silver, with Aditi Ashok and Diksha Dagar completing the team.It rounded articles.body: El futuro empieza aquí. Con esta frase en un cartel y al ritmo de la canción Superestrella de Aitana comenzó este sábado en el Centro de Alto Rendimiento de Madrid el sexto Draft Paralímpico que organiza el Comité Paralímpico Español y que cuenta con el apoyo de CaixaBank. Un total de 37 niños y jóvenes con discapacidad, de entre 10 y 28 años, se mostraban muy ilusionados con la oportunidad. Sus caras antes de empezar la jornada así lo reflejaban. Lo que se busca en esta actividad es conocer sus aptitudes e introducirlos en el deporte que mejor se ajuste a sus perfiles. Como dijo Francisco Botía, director general del Comité Paralímpico Español, quizá entre ellos se encuentre 'Nuestra próxima estrella', nombre del programa que permite la detección y captación de talento joven en toda España y que busca dar con quienes releven en el futuro a Teresa Perales, Susana Rodríguez o Ricardo Ten. Desde las 10:00 horas, los jóvenes con discapacidad física, visual o parálisis cerebral realizaron diferentes pruebas y juegos con el objetivo de medir sus capacidades. Por la tarde probarán algunos de los ocho deportes que se les ofrece: atletismo, bádminton, ciclismo, escalada, natación, piragüismo, tenis de mesa y triatlón. Después, escucharon los testimonios de grandes figuras del deporte paralímpico como la triatleta Susana Rodríguez, que acaba de conquistar su octavo título mundial, la nadadora Beatriz Lérida, campeona europea en septiembre en Kocaeli (Turquía) y el esquiador Javier Marcos, que debutó en los Juegos Paralímpicos de Milán-Cortina este mismo año. "Para CaixaBank es un orgullo y una oportunidad el potenciar y acompañar a los niños y jóvenes que quieran probar el deporte. No hemos venido a ganar medallas sino a dar un primer paso en el camino", dijo Carlos Candeal, director de Banca de Instituciones de CaixaBank en Madrid. "Queremos que descubráis nuevas posibilidades y os marchéis con ganas de practicar deporte. Estamos para ayudaros a encontrar vuestro camino. Quizá alguno de vosotros llegue a representar a España en unos Juegos, pero hoy el objetivo es encontrar un deporte que os guste. El talento necesita entrenamiento y constancia, pero también oportunidades", añadió Botía. La jornada comenzó con los participantes haciendo un calentamiento conjunto antes de pasar por diferentes estaciones de evaluación. Mediante pruebas y juegos adaptados se analizan capacidades como la fuerza, la velocidad y aceleración, la resistencia aeróbica, la flexibilidad, el equilibrio y la coordinación. Los resultados serán analizados por el equipo técnico del Comité Paralímpico Español y por los responsables y los seleccionadores de los diferentes programas de promesas paralímpicas, que seleccionarán para sus deportes a aquellos deportistas con mayor proyección. "En mi caso, la idea es hacer unas pruebas dirigidas hacia la resistencia y de los que veamos que tengan esas capacidades fisiológicas y esa atracción hacia el ciclismo, que prueben nuestro deporte. Es un evento lleno de ilusión porque se inician. Hemos detectado unos cuantos casos que poquito a poco se van metiendo en la competición. El relevo es una necesidad imperante y este tipo de iniciativas son necesarias para conseguirlo. Sería bonito que en Brisbane 2032 podamos hacer una foto y decir: "A ese chavalín le conocí hace muchos años en un Relevo paralímpico", señala Begoña Luis, seleccionadora nacional de ciclismo. La madrileña, además, busca que les guste la velocidad y la independencia que da la bicicleta, pero "también es importante que cuenten con el apoyo de sus familias", señala. También muy atenta a las pruebas estaba Celia Maestre, responsable del programa de Relevo Paralímpico en la Comunidad Valenciana y guía de David Casinos en los Juegos de Atenas 2004, Pekín 2008 y Londres 2012. "El relevo generacional es lo que más nos está costando. No es fácil. El deporte paralímpico es deporte de élite y llegar a esa élite es complicado. Iniciativas como ésta son fundamentales porque gracias a ellas conocen el mundo paralímpico, prueban los deportes y ponemos ya la primera piedra en el camino", explica. "Lo ideal es que encuentren su deporte y que, además, puedan practicarlo cerca de casa. Intentamos orientarles hacia el que se ajuste más a su discapacidad", añade. Por la tarde, durante la segunda parte de la jornada, los participantes tendrán la oportunidad de probar las ocho modalidades deportivas.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally: Golden run in hockey, cricket, wrestling, archery takes India into top 4
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India moved up to fourth place in the Asian Games 2026 medal tally after a big medal-winning day on Saturday.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India moved up to fourth place in the Asian Games 2026 medal tally after a big medal-winning day on Saturday. India added five gold medals across wrestling, golf, hockey, cricket and archery to take their overall tally to 85 medals - 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze.India's men's hockey team provided the final gold of the day, beating Malaysia 5-1 to retain the Asian Games title and secure a place at the 2028 Olympics. India also won gold through Aman Sehrawat in wrestling, Pranavi Urs in golf, the men's cricket team and Kumkum Mohod in women's individual recurve archery.India pip Uzbekistan to go fourthIndia's five gold medals on Saturday made the biggest difference to their position in the table. From 18 gold medals and fifth place earlier in the day, India finished Saturday with 21 gold medals and moved into fourth.The five golds came from five different sports, underlining the spread of India's medal-winning performances across the Games.With 85 medals in total, India are just one medal behind Kazakhstan's 84, but their much higher gold count puts them comfortably ahead of Kazakhstan in the standings.Asian Games 2026 medal tally: Top 10 countries 1. India's tally stands at 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, for a total of 85 medals. The five golds came in wrestling, golf, cricket, archery and men's hockey. The hockey gold was particularly significant as India beat Malaysia 5-1 to retain the men's title. Earlier, the women's hockey team had also won gold, giving India a historic men's and women's hockey double at the same Asian Games. articles.title: Connor McDavid chose a $25 million extension over a massive raise to protect Edmonton Oilers’ Stanley Cup window and keep hockey’s biggest superstar focused on winning in Edmonton
articles.summary: Connor McDavid has signed a two-year, $25 million contract extension with the Edmonton Oilers, prioritizing the team's Stanley Cup ambitions over a larger salary. This decision supports roster flexibility and aims for championship glory before he becomes a free agent in 2028.
articles.body: Connor McDavid made a big decision about his Edmonton Oilers future when he signed a two-year, $25-million contract extension instead of going for a much bigger salary. The contract, which begins with the 2026-27 season, keeps his average annual value at $12.5 million, the same as the eight-year deal he signed before the 2018-19 season.That was notable in that a player of McDavid’s stature did not have his salary change. Since being taken No. 1 overall in the 2015 NHL Draft, the Edmonton Oilers captain has developed into one of the NHL’s most decorated stars. His decision gives Edmonton more money to work with as the organization tries to build a roster that can compete for the Stanley Cup.Details on Connor McDavid NHL contract extension Connor McDavid’s extension structure allows the Edmonton Oilers to be more flexible with their roster decisions. His $12.5 million annual cap hit has remained intact as the league's salary landscape has shifted, allowing Edmonton to use its available resources on other areas of the roster.The flexibility, general manager Stan Bowman said, gives the organization more options as it evaluates trades, contracts and future roster upgrades. Around the same time, the Oilers signed defenseman Jake Walman to a seven-year, $49 million extension, which further drives home how important financial flexibility can be in building a competitive roster.The two-year term also provides a clear timetable for both sides. McDavid is signed through 2027-28 and can become an unrestricted free agent after that. That gives Edmonton a clear window to build on the current core and pursue its championship hopes.Connor McDavid keeps Stanley Cup pursuit centralMcDavid has made winning the Stanley Cup the top priority of his career in Edmonton, and the new deal reflects that priority. The Oilers were in the back-to-back Stanley Cup Finals before losing to the Florida Panthers, as the franchise is still searching for its first championship since 1990.The deal also keeps McDavid with a number of key members of Edmonton's core. The captain is in some notable company with Leon Draisaitl, Zach Hyman, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Evan Bouchard as the organization continues to build the roster.McDavid already has most of the big individual awards available to an NHL player. He is a three-time Hart Trophy winner, four-time Ted Lindsay Award winner and five-time Art Ross Trophy winner. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy in 2024 as the playoffs’ most valuable player, leading all players in postseason awards.The final major accomplishment is the Stanley Cup, something McDavid and the Oilers have continued to chase together.Edmonton Oilers face pressure during McDavid windowThe extension provides stability, but it also makes the coming seasons more meaningful. Edmonton can’t view this deal as a long-term fix that relieves pressure on the organization. Instead, the contract gives the Oilers a relatively short window to continue building around their captain.The situation gained even more importance after Edmonton was eliminated by the Anaheim Ducks in the first round of the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs. That was the earliest of Edmonton’s postseason exits since 2021, when the Oilers reached the Stanley Cup Final in back-to-back seasons, according to NHL.com.McDavid is still very much in the team’s plans. During the 2025-26 regular season, he paced the NHL with 138 points (48 goals, 90 assists) while Draisaitl had 97 points in 65 games.So the new contract means something more than just another notch on McDavid’s career timeline. The deal allows the Edmonton Oilers some financial flexibility, with their captain staying in Edmonton through the 2027-28 season. For McDavid, the choice keeps the focus on the same goal that has defined his Edmonton tenure: Building another chance to compete for the Stanley Cup.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: La autocrítica de Néstor Lorenzo tras la sorpresiva caída de Selección Colombia contra Paraguay
articles.body: La Selección Colombia analiza con lupa los recientes compromisos de preparación en territorio estadounidense. Tras un tropiezo futbolístico frente a Paraguay dirigida por Gustavo Alfaro, las miradas y críticas se volcaron sobre el funcionamiento del equipo y la falta de claridad en el terreno de juego. Sin embargo, en rueda de prensa, el director técnico Néstor Lorenzo asumió una postura de serenidad y autocrítica, pidiendo paciencia a la afición. Durante sus declaraciones ante los medios, el estratega argentino dejó claro que el plantel atraviesa una fase de transición y recambio generacional tras un año de alta exigencia competitiva. Lorenzo enfatizó en que este tipo de compromisos amistosos sirven precisamente para probar alternativas y evaluar nuevas piezas en la nómina. "Ahora estamos en una etapa de construcción, tenemos que decir la verdad: no está el equipo armado y faltaron muchos jugadores que van a ser parte de este ciclo. Hemos dejado que se recuperen de un año muy intenso. Queremos ir incorporando y ver qué jugadores van a estar para tener dentro del proceso", afirmó el estratega. El técnico detalló los puntos concretos donde la Selección Colombia evidenció falencias futbolísticas durante los 90 minutos: Lorenzo concluyó su análisis recordando que los criterios de convocatoria siguen enfocados en priorizar el rendimiento deportivo combinado con los valores humanos dentro del grupo. Aunque las derrotas en partidos de preparación generan inquietud en la hinchada, el cuerpo técnico mantiene el foco en consolidar la estructura del equipo de cara a los retos oficiales del calendario internacional.

articles.title: Cale Makar, Connor Bedard and Kirill Kaprizov are reshaping NHL money as hockey enters a new era of $75 million-plus contracts
articles.summary: Explore how Cale Makar, Connor Bedard, and Kirill Kaprizov are transforming NHL contracts with groundbreaking deals surpassing $75 million, reflecting the league's evolving financial landscape.
articles.body: The NHL’s biggest contracts are entering a new financial phase, with star players commanding numbers that would have been tough to imagine just a few seasons ago. Cale Makar, Connor Bedard and Kirill Kaprizov are leading that shift, each signing a contract worth at least $75 million.The growth is also being fueled by the league’s growing salary cap. The cap is $104 million for 2026-27 and is projected to hit $113.5 million for 2027-28, allowing teams more flexibility to get creative with long-term contracts.Cale Makar, Connor Bedard and Kirill Kaprizov lead NHL’s contract marketCale Makar has taken the NHL salary market to a new level at the top end. The Colorado Avalanche blueliner inked an eight-year, $163.2 million extension in August 2026 with an average annual value of $20.4 million. The contract kicks in with the 2027-28 season and is the richest deal in NHL history.Makar’s deal also made him the first NHL player to surpass the $20 million per year salary mark. His contract is a big upgrade from the six-year, $54 million deal he signed with the Avalanche beforehand.Timing is important because the salary cap is expected to be $113.5 million in 2027-28. So Makar’s new cap hit will eat up a large chunk of Colorado’s available payroll room.PlayerTeamContractAAVCale MakarColorado Avalanche$163.2M / 8 years$20.4MKirill KaprizovMinnesota Wild$136M / 8 years$17MConnor BedardChicago Blackhawks$75M / 5 years$15MConnor Bedard adds another big contract to the ever-growing market the Chicago Blackhawks center inked a five-year, $75 million extension in July of 2026 that has a $15 million AAV.Bedard entered the deal as Chicago's leading scorer in all three of his first NHL seasons. His $10.5 million cap hit through 2025-26 gives the Blackhawks long-term financial certainty around the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 NHL Draft.Kirill Kaprizov was a big piece of the cap gymnastics before Makar and Bedard signed their latest deals. The Minnesota Wild forward signed an eight-year, $136 million extension in 2025 with a $17 million AAV starting in 2026-27.It was the highest annual average in NHL history at the time. Makar has since exceeded that level, and Bedard’s $15 million AAV reflects the market differentials at various stages of a player’s career.Kaprizov’s contract also came at a time when the league was preparing for back-to-back salary-cap increases, giving an early glimpse of how higher league revenues and greater payroll flexibility could impact negotiations for elite players.The deals together are reshaping the top of the NHL pay scale. Cale Makar, Kirill Kaprizov and Connor Bedard are among the players who have set financial benchmarks that future negotiations will no doubt be compared to.The challenge for NHL teams will be how to balance these record-setting individual contracts with their ever more competitive roster-building demands. The increasing cap gives players more room to grab a bigger piece of league-wide revenue.The $75 million contract is not an extraordinary ceiling anymore. articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s Excel connection raises questions as Linda Cohn challenges WNBA commissioner search safeguards
articles.summary: The NBA has hired Excel Search & Advisory to help find Cathy Engelbert’s successor as WNBA commissioner, but the choice has already raised questions about
articles.body: The NBA has hired Excel Search & Advisory to help find Cathy Engelbert’s successor as WNBA commissioner, but the choice has already raised questions about possible conflicts of interest. Excel’s parent company, Excel Sports Management, represents WNBA stars Caitlin Clark and Napheesa Collier. Former ESPN host Linda Cohn has now asked how the company will keep its player representation work separate from the executive search as the league prepares for a major leadership change.Linda Cohn questions Excel’s role in the WNBA commissioner searchCohn focused on the connection between Excel and Caitlin Clark, whose rise has brought major attention to the WNBA. She said the situation deserves clear answers because the same wider company represents players while its search arm is helping identify the person who could lead the league.“Caitlin Clark isn’t just another client,” Cohn said in a video posted on her YouTube channel. “We are talking about a player whose arrival helped accelerate an extraordinary period of attention and business growth around this league. And now an arm of the company that represents her is helping identify the next commissioner of that league.”Cohn also pointed to Excel’s representation of other WNBA players, including Napheesa Collier, and said the league should explain how the two sides of the business will be kept apart.“So I think there’s a completely fair question to ask here. How separate are these operations? What safeguards are in place?” Cohn said. “Who inside Excel Search and Advisory has access to information about these candidates, and who doesn’t, for that matter? Is there a firewall between the executive search business and the agents representing WNBA players? … These are questions that need answers.”The concern is about the process, not a claim that Excel has acted improperly. Public reports have not established that information from the commissioner search has been shared with Excel’s player representation business.Excel Search & Advisory has WNBA ties as Cathy Engelbert prepares to leaveExcel Search & Advisory is the executive search arm of Excel Sports Management. According to Sports Business Journal, the NBA hired the firm to lead the search, while NBA Commissioner Adam Silver will make the final decision on Engelbert’s replacement.The timing is important because Engelbert announced on September 4 that she will retire at the end of 2026 after seven years as commissioner. The WNBA said her tenure included major growth in viewership, attendance, League Pass subscriptions, merchandise sales, sponsorship revenue and franchise values.Excel also has business ties with several WNBA teams. Reports say the company has worked on jersey patch partnerships involving the Atlanta Dream, Los Angeles Sparks and Dallas Wings, while its executive search business has helped professional sports organizations with senior hiring.That makes the company familiar with the league and its wider business structure, but it also explains why Cohn wants more clarity about how the search will be handled.For now, Excel’s job is to identify and vet candidates. The final choice remains with Adam Silver and the NBA Board of Governors. The WNBA has not publicly detailed specific safeguards for separating Excel’s search work from its player representation business.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Most centuries at No. 5 in ODI cricket history: Full list of batters
articles.summary: With KL Rahul scoring his 4th century at no.5, here's the list of ODI batters with most tons at the number.
articles.body:
Former Indian all-rounder Yuvraj Singh holds the record for most ODI hundreds at No. 5, with seven.

South Africa 's AB de Villiers is second with six, scored in just 42 innings.

KL Rahul has four hundreds at No. 5 and averages 68.58 in the position.

KL Rahul is slowly becoming one of the best at No. 5.

KL Rahul has reached four ODI hundreds at No. 5, a mark that places him among the most productive batters ever to bat in that position. The milestone raises a wider question: who has scored the most centuries at No. 5 in ODI cricket history?

Yuvraj Singh leads with seven, ahead of AB de Villiers on six. Six batters sit on five, and Rahul is one of six on four. Here is the full list of batters with at least four hundreds at No. 5.

Who has scored the most centuries at No. 5 in ODI cricket?

Yuvraj Singh holds the record with seven hundreds at No. 5, scored across 92 innings between 2000 and 2017. His 3,040 runs came at an average of 39.48 and a strike rate of 87.58, with a highest score of 139.

AB de Villiers is second with six, and his numbers stand out for efficiency. He needed only 42 innings, averaged 77.96 and scored at 108.97 runs per 100 balls, with a best of 162*. Yuvraj took more than twice as many innings.

Six batters follow on five hundreds each: Charith Asalanka, Tom Latham, Eoin Morgan, Shakib Al Hasan, Sikandar Raza and Andrew Symonds. Raza got there in 54 innings, the fewest of the six, while Shakib needed 132.

Most centuries at No. 5 in ODI cricket history: Full list

The table below ranks every batter with a minimum of four hundreds at No. 5 in ODIs.

What is KL Rahul's record at No. 5 in ODIs?

Rahul has scored 1,646 runs in 36 innings at No. 5 between 2017 and 2026, with 12 not-outs. His average of 68.58 is the second-best among all 14 batters in the table, behind only de Villiers.

He has also scored quickly, at a strike rate of 103.19, and his highest score in the position is an unbeaten 129. Alongside his four centuries, he has 10 fifties, and he has not been dismissed for a duck in any of those 36 innings.

Of the six batters with four centuries, only Milind Kumar reached the mark in fewer innings. Klaasen took 41, Miller 43, Collingwood 80, and Dhoni 83. Rahul now needs three more to equal Yuvraj's record, a target that looks distant but not out of reach at a hundred roughly every nine innings.

articles.title: Washington defense facing tough task in USC's explosive offense
articles.summary: Washington's defense will have to switch gears from last week, as it faces one of the country's most potent passing attacks.
articles.body:
As the Washington Huskies prepare for their second Big Ten game, on the road at USC, Ryan Walters' defense will face a much different challenge than it did against Minnesota. While the Golden Gophers offense was able to secure the victory thanks to time of possession, chunk yardage, and a much more methodical brand of football, coach Lincoln Riley and the Trojans present a very different look.

Led by fifth-year quarterback Jayden Maiava, the USC offense averages 325 passing yards per game, compared to Minnesota's 258. Although the passing game is the centerpiece of Riley's offense, the Trojans also present a much more explosive running game, averaging 164 yards on the ground, whereas the Gophers average just 119.

"His development of quarterbacks is elite, and he has another elite quarterback in Maiava; he's big, 6-foot-4, 230 [pounds], can run around, they don't ask him to run a ton, but he'll keep you honest with his legs," Walters said on Tuesday.

"Elite arm talent; he can make all the throws, he's extremely accurate, and he gives his guys a chance to go make plays even when there's tight coverage. And he's got guys that can go make plays for him, especially when they're in space. So, it'll be a collective effort defensively to get stops and get off the field to get the ball back to our offense, because possessions are going to be a premium on Saturday."

After giving up 21 points in the first half of last week's loss, the Huskies limited quarterback Drake Lindsey and the Gopher offense to just six points in the second half. While second-half adjustments kept Washington in the fight late, falling behind by multiple possessions against an offense as potent as USC's is a recipe for disaster.

Despite coaching in the Big Ten since 2021, either as UW or Illinois' defensive coordinator or in his stint as Purdue's head coach, Walters has never crossed paths with the Trojans. Out of the nine possessions USC had in its loss to Oregon, the Trojans scored on five of them, including three of five in the second half. In order for the Huskies to stay in the fight on the road against a ranked opponent, getting stops is a must, and taking advantage of them is even more crucial.

While the opposing offense may pose much different challenges than last week, the message remains the same for Walters' defense: create havoc, play disciplined, and get off the field.

articles.title: Penn State postgame report card: Grading Nittany Lions vs. Northwestern
articles.summary: Penn State football suffered a disastrous loss to Northwestern, leading to failing grades across the roster.
articles.body:
Penn State had a great opportunity to get revenge in the best possible way: winning in Northwestern's new stadium almost a year after a stunning loss sent their entire season in a tailspin. Instead, this may have been Northwestern's coming out party, as the Nittany Lions suffered a much worse fate than last year's. Now, a season filled with budding potential has been lost before it even truly began. Here is what the postgame report card looks after their glaringly terrible loss to Northwestern .

This was supposed to be a performance that showed that Rocco Becht was able to move forward from the single worst career start. To prove that he was still every bit the most experienced college football QB in the nation. Instead, he was no better than last week, with the same mistakes popping up in an alarming manner. At this point, Penn State fans have to wonder if this is more than just missing what Koby Howard brought to the offense and whether or not this is the real Rocco Becht, someone who struggles against the more physical defenses in the Big Ten. Sure, his stats look inflated by his fourth-quarter production, but it is disturbing if this is the only time and situation of the game he's comfortable operating in. If this continues to be the case, prepare for yet another rough season in Happy Valley.

A low grade always seems to be in the cards for this running back room who was supposed to provide a spark to this offense due to their differing traits. And yet somehow, they have found a way to lower their expectations. It is absolutely appalling when the leading rusher on your team only has 19 yards. There is simply nothing redeemable about that stat. This has now not just become an issue of the function of this offense, but whether or not these backs are good enough for this conference.

Well, at least Chase Sowell showed some heart. While some Penn State fans are holding out hope that Howard's return can fix this mess, the fact the receivers who they brought in to produce have failed to do so is damning in its own right. Howard was a great revelation to start the season, but in all reality, it was the Iowa State transfers who were supposed to define. They haven't and as a result, I see no reason to believe that this offense will click in any subsequent game.

This is clearly not the defense that we saw over the first three weeks of the defense and quite frankly might not be for the rest of the season. Consider this: Northwestern rushed for 237 yards in the first half alone. Joseph Himon II had 137 of those yards. In the first half. And he was not even their leading rusher. That would be Caleb Komolafe, who had 188 yards. Ultimately, Northwestern ended up rushing for 415 yards for a shocking 8 yards per carry. That is simply unacceptable for a defense predicated on getting its linebackers close to the line of scrimmage to help get in the backfield. Right now, it looks like the first three weeks were just a facade.

Not even Ryan Barker could get points on the board for this offense, which was thought to be a gimme. And it's never a good thing when you send your punter out seven times, as Penn State did Nathan Tiyce . The less said about the special teams coverage and the lack of discipline in that regard, the better.

The quiet thoughts about Campbell from last week's loss are now becoming ever louder for Penn State fans. This was supposed to be the guy who made amends to the culture of this team and, most importantly, get them back to national relevance. It is now clear why he was not the Nittany Lion's first choice for the job. Sure, you can say the players he brought into the program might not be up to snuff. But with Penn State's heightened resources compared to Iowa State's, he was supposed to attract more talent. Now, that talent looks like it will struggle through a lost season when the coach who believed in them could not find a way to bring it all together. Alarm bells are well and truly ringing when it comes to Matt Campbell.

Not even the casual Penn State fans could have foreseen how low this team has sunk. In two consecutive seasons now, they've had two embarrassing losses to start their Big Ten campaign. While this team has the chance to somewhat rewrite this season's narrative, there is no reason to believe that they will based on these past two performances. What looked to be intriguing opportunities for statement wins against USC and Michigan before the season have now turned into potential nightmares about how this team will look.

Penn State will return home to take on the No. 18 USC Trojans for their annual White Out game. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 PM ET on Saturday, October 10 on NBC.

articles.title: Game Thread: White Sox at Guardians ALDS Game 1
articles.summary: It’s the South Siders’ first time in a second playoff round since 2005, and we all know what happened then
articles.body:
It's showdown at high noon (Central), as two teams that played as even a regular season series as can be match up in an American League Division Series.

The White Sox won the season series, 7-6, with seven of the games being determined by one run, and only one by more than three. The teams were so close in talent that the Sox scored 58 runs and the Guardians 57 over the course of the season. Of course, the old cliché about throwing out the record books pops up now, but sometimes a peek at the books gives a pretty good hint at what's to come.

What's to come today is Hagen Smith throwing for the White Sox, just as he started the Wild Card series. He went a scoreless three innings on just 38 pitches in that one, giving up two hits and no walks and getting one strikeout. He faced Cleveland three times during the regular season and they hit just .105 against him, albeit with a .320 OBP due to Smith walking six of 25 batters.

The Sox are quiet about who will follow in a quasi-bullpen game, but against Houston it went Jordan Hicks, Sean Newcomb, David Sandlin and Grant Taylor. It may be mostly southpaws today, given the Guardians lefty-heavy lineup.

There's no bullpen game for Cleveland, that's for sure. With the advantage of a first-round bye, the Guardians are marching out their ace, lefty Parker Messick. Messick went 12-9 with a 2.56 ERA and 193 strikeouts in 186 innings in his official rookie season. In four starts against the Sox he was 2-1 with a 2.81 ERA, giving up a .198/.245/.385 slash line.

Last time out against them he gave up three runs in six innings, all of them scoring on a Tommy Pham homer, so it's no surprise that Pham is in the starting lineup again today, in the 5-slot.

Smith and friends face a Cleveland lineup that came alive in September, enough so to take the AL Central title from the Sox. Will the long break thanks to the opening-round bye give them needed rest, especially for José Ramirez's hand, or will they be rusty? Only The Shadow knows.

First pitch is scheduled right at noon Central on a perfect fall day — mostly sunny, mid-60s and light wind in from right. Tube coverage is on TBS, truTV, Univision/TUDN and HBO Max, while ESPN 1000 has the radio side.

articles.title: Texans STC Frank Ross on the intention during final kickoff vs Colts
articles.summary: Houston Texans special teams coordinator Frank Ross explains the intention on the final kickoff versus the Indianapolis Colts in Week 3.
articles.body:
Small decisions players make often win games and coaches look smart. One of those decisions for the Houston Texans against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 3 was the decision to kick the ball into the end zone for a touchback on Indianapolis' final drive, where they scored the game-winning field goal.

Special teams coordinator Frank Ross addressed the intention of that final kickoff ahead of Houston's Week 4 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

"Depending on the situation, we're always aiming for the goal line and really being able to know that, if it goes in, no worries. If it stays out, great, let's cover it up, depending on the call in the game," Ross said. "I know Coach [DeMeco Ryans] referred to that. For all of the strategy and the statistics of the whole dynamic kickoff, the farther you have to run gives your coverage the better chance. Nobody's better than [K Ka'imi] Fairbairn in putting that thing at the inch yard line and making them. Those goal line decisions, making that returner, we have been a benefactor of seeing some of those poor decisions by returners to, 'Wait, where am I', and then they run. You just gained time. Knowing when and where a forced kick in the field of play, a green light to try and put it directly on the goal line, if it touchbacks, live to fight another day."

Fairbairn's kick was a rare mistake by him, as Houston wanted to pin the Colts back deep to make it harder to get into field goal range. That play alone potentially cost the Texans their first win of the season.

This was also the second game in a row where Houston had a major special teams miscue with their botched field goal attempt in Week 2 against the Cincinnati Bengals .

If they are going to win their game against the Cowboys, the Texans will need to avoid these kinds of mistakes. They also desperately need this win to avoid dropping to 0-4. There has only been one team in NFL history, the 1992 Los Angeles Chargers, that have started 0-4 and made the playoffs.

articles.title: Cowboys Face Major Setback With Dual Injuries Amid Joey Porter Jr. Update
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are struggling to fix a defense that ranks 30th in total yards allowed and has zero interceptions. Heading into a Week 4 matchup against t...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are struggling to fix a defense that ranks 30th in total yards allowed and has zero interceptions. Heading into a Week 4 matchup against the Houston Texans this Sunday, Jerry Jones' 1-2 franchise desperately needs a spark.

Right after trading for defensive back Joey Porter Jr. to help the secondary, the team's final injury report brought a severe dual setback. Dallas officially ruled out two defensive starters, forcing a complete defensive reshuffle right before kickoff.

Cowboys rule out key players as Joey Porter Jr. prepares for Texans debut

The bad news centers on cornerback Cobie Durant and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who both missed practice all week with hamstring injuries. Durant hurt his hamstring in Week 2 and will sit out a second straight game, while Overshown will miss his third straight contest. Rookie Jaishawn Barham continues to fill in at inside linebacker.

Pro Football Talk's Charean Williams highlighted the defensive stakes on X, writing , "CB Cobie Durant, LB DeMarvion Overshown ruled out, but Malik Hooker returns."

He added , "The Cowboys expect cornerback Joey Porter to play on Sunday in Houston. That's good news since they won't have cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring)… Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) will also miss another week."

To bridge the coverage gap, Dallas finalized a trade on Wednesday , sending a 2028 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers to land Porter.

The 26-year-old cornerback missed the first three games of the season due to a back issue during a contract stalemate. He is in the final year of his rookie contract, and reports indicate Dallas does not plan to negotiate an extension this season.

Since Porter has not played a snap this year, the coaching staff plans to manage his workload on Sunday. Executive vice president Stephen Jones expressed optimism about the acquisition on 105.3 The Fan, stating , "We actually think Joey Porter will get snaps." Defensive coordinator Christian Parker echoed that excitement, labeling Porter a "boundary eraser" at corner.

"He fits well," Parker said . "He's a high-level coverage player, plays with great length. He has a lot of experience against a lot of high-level receivers, so we have evidence about how he does in that environment. Really excited about having him here."

Meanwhile, the winless Houston Texans (0-3) received an offensive boost. Star receiver Nico Collins took part in all team drills on Friday and carries no injury concerns after missing the last two games. Despite their winless record, the Texans enter the rivalry matchup as 3-point favorites over the 1-2 Cowboys.

articles.title: 'I want to discover Manchester' - Olid hunts recommendations
articles.summary: Manchester United manager Eva Olid says she is "asking for recommendations" as she prepares to look around the city for the first time during the internation...
articles.body:
Manchester United manager Eva Olid says she is "asking for recommendations" as she prepares to look around the city for the first time during the international break.

The Spaniard replaced Marc Skinner two months ago after leaving Hearts but told BBC Sport that she has been so busy working, she has yet to explore her new home.

Having beaten rivals Liverpool on Saturday, United now have a fortnight's break from action while international play-offs for the World Cup take place and Olid is determined to make the most of it.

"I didn't stop from when I arrived!" she said. "Home, work, home, work. My parents are here, my family are here and now I want to discover Manchester."

United's women's team play most of their home matches at Leigh Sports Village, approximately 12 miles west of central Manchester, while they train on the same site as the men at Carrington in Trafford.

Despite great success in the Scottish Women's Premier League, Olid arrived at United as an unknown quantity in English football.

It was a difficult start too, losing to London City Lionesses on the opening night of the Women's Super League season before being thrashed 5-0 at home by Chelsea a week later - managing just two shots on target combined in those games.

However, drawing at Arsenal was promising, and now four straight wins across the WSL and League Cup with 18 goals scored suggests her philosophy is starting to get through.

"I am so happy for the players - they deserve it," she said. "We have started to click in a lot of things and they fight for each other.

"But there is still a lot to improve. We created chances, but our last pass and our finishing needs to be better. That will come."

Liverpool counterpart Gareth Taylor was less impressed with Olid's tactics, having seen his side's encouraging start to the season stunted by two defeats in their past three.

"They were very direct and we fell into their trap," he said. "Their goalkeeper was literally kicking out of her hands.

"We have got to be braver and there are lessons to learn. This was the first time where we have not been a good reflection of ourselves."
authors: Joe Bradshaw - BBC Sport senior journalist
