The Los Angeles Rams are going to be without Myles Garrett for a few more weeks, as he was placed on injured reserve after Week 1's loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

He'll be forced to miss at least four weeks, meaning he's already been ruled out through Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season. But beyond that, he's available to come back. The only question is, when will he be good to come off IR?

Well, according to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic , the Rams actually got some good news when the "worst-case" scenario for Garrett was revealed. The reason why that's the case is that his worst possible return date is only six weeks after his injury.

How Myles Garrett's worst-case return date is good news for Rams

"Though there was a report last week Garrett could be out up to six weeks, one source views that as a worst-case scenario," Jones writes. "A second team source believes Garrett will make his return by Oct. 25 against the Raiders ."

Garrett is going to miss four weeks at minimum. That means he'll be out through Week 5. Afterwards, he's eligible to come off IR for the Rams.

While there is reporting that suggests he could be back as soon as Week 6, there isn't any confirmation that it's the week he'll be back.

Fortunately for the Rams, however, the worst-case scenario with Garrett's return being revealed as six weeks missed, or a Week 8 return, is not a bad scenario at all.

While the Rams would surely prefer to have Garrett back before then, a six-week injury being the "worst-case scenario" for Garrett, as Jones shared from a Rams source, is some good news.

The sooner he returns, the better. He can be back starting in Week 6, but even if he's forced to sit longer, this report indicates it would be a surprise if he's not back by Week 8 at the latest.

That's still a ways away, but all things considered, a six-week absence for Garrett at the start of the season being the "worst-case scenario" is not actually that bad of an outcome.

articles.title: Browns’ 3-1 Start Has Fans Asking If Todd Monken, Andrew Berry Deserve More Trust
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns had plenty to answer for when the season started. A new coach, a new offense and another quarterback decision left little room for mista...
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns had plenty to answer for when the season started. A new coach, a new offense and another quarterback decision left little room for mistakes after last year's 5-12 finish.

Then Jacksonville turned the opener into a 34-10 loss. Since then, Cleveland has beaten Tampa Bay, Carolina and Pittsburgh to reach 3-1 and take the early AFC North lead.

Browns fans are starting to look differently at the new regime

That start has led Earl D. Mauldin to question the people running the team. Speaking with Spencer German, Mauldin asked whether Todd Monken , Andrew Berry and the Haslam family have earned more trust after what Cleveland has shown through four games.

"I'm wondering now…have at least Todd Monken, maybe Andrew Berry and the Haslam family…have they earned a little bit more trust from this fan base when you see how the first four games of this season have played out," Mauldin said .

The question has a clear reason behind it. Cleveland did not panic after the Jacksonville loss, and Monken's team has won three straight close games. Deshaun Watson has also led a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter in each of those three victories.

Todd Monken has changed the Browns without fixing everything

The biggest change has come on defense. Cleveland recorded five sacks and forced two turnovers against Pittsburgh, including Grant Delpit's interception on the Steelers' final possession.

The offense has done enough to win, but problems remain. Cleveland has scored 81 points through four games, an average of 20.3 per game that ranks 21st in the NFL. Discipline is another concern after the Browns committed 12 penalties for 88 yards against Pittsburgh.

Berry's work is also beginning to show through the young players he added. Rookie receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have taken on larger roles, and Cleveland's official site said both are developing into key parts of the passing game after Thursday's win.

Still, those promising signs do not settle the larger questions surrounding the front office. A 3-1 record can quickly change the mood, but Cleveland must prove these early wins are the foundation for lasting success rather than just one strong month.

For now, Mauldin's question has a reasonable starting point. The Browns have given fans three straight wins to consider, but the rest of the season will determine how much trust that record deserves.

articles.title: Colts Make Late Roster Move on Keenan Allen Ahead of Commanders London Showdown
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are having a poor start to the 2026 NFL season. The team has lost the first two games of the season, and has only one win in the three...
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are having a poor start to the 2026 NFL season. The team has lost the first two games of the season, and has only one win in the three games they have played so far this season.

While the Colts are preparing for an epic showdown against the Washington Commanders in London, a late update on one player has been announced.

Colts rule out Keenan Allen for Commanders game

The Colts have announced that wide receiver Keenan Allen has been downgraded to out for their Week 4 matchup against the Commanders at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Allen is dealing with a groin injury, and practiced on a limited basis earlier in the week before being listed as a non-participant on October 1, 2026. He was then carrying a questionable designation into the weekend before the recent update that he will not be playing. This is in contrast to the previous communication that no players will be ruled out for the game.

Allen was signed by the Colts in August on a one-year deal worth up to $8.32 million. The six-time Pro Bowler last played for the Los Angeles Chargers in 2025. His absence compounds existing depth issues at the position ahead of a crucial clash. Alec Pierce remains sidelined with a heel injury, leaving Josh Downs as the primary receiving option. Additional targets are expected to shift toward Darius Slayton, Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks, and tight end Tyler Warren.

Allen has recorded 13 receptions for 100 yards and one touchdown so far in the 2026 season. He has played in all three games. The 34-year-old previously worked with Colts head coach Shane Steichen for several seasons when he was with the Chargers. He is expected to return for the Week 5 contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers on October 11, 2026.

Steichen also talked about one particular opponent player ahead of the Commanders clash.

Colts' Shane Steichen talks about Commanders' Marcus Mariota

Steichen was asked about Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota ahead of facing him in London. According to The Athletic's James Boyd , he said, "He's won a lot of games in the league. A lot of respect for him. Heard a lot of great things about him as the person as well. But very mobile, can make plays with his legs. Very good in the pocket, too, as well."

Mariota has played in 2 games so far this season, only starting one of them. He has completed 30 of 47 passes for 294 yards and 4 touchdowns with no interceptions. He is going to start for the Commanders as they face the Colts at the international game in London.

The Indianapolis Colts will now prepare to face off against the Washington Commanders, and will hope that Keenan Allen's absence will not affect them.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford, Rams Receive Crucial Puka Nacua News After Aaron Donald Ruled Out Against Eagles
articles.summary: Aaron Donald’s return was as dramatic as it get. It didn’t come as a sudden shock to the fans rather Aaron Donald was teasing about his return on social medi...
articles.body:
Aaron Donald's return was as dramatic as it get. It didn't come as a sudden shock to the fans rather Aaron Donald was teasing about his return on social media for a while before returning after three years.

But now after Week 3 of 2026, the defensive tackle is injured getting himself unavailable for Week 4. But Los Angeles Rams have something to cheer about as their wide receiver Puka Nacua gets back from injury.

Aaron Donald gets injured after return but Puka Nacua returns

Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles because of back soreness. In the two games he has played this season, Donald has been on the field for about 56% of the defensive snaps, showing that the Rams have been carefully managing his workload rather than deploying him as an every-down force.

The soreness surfaced after the Rams' Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos. While the team has not released extensive medical details, the timing suggests the physical toll of playing at an elite level again after time away may be a factor. Rams head coach Sean McVay addressed the decision directly and thoughtfully on Friday. He made clear that the choice to hold Donald out was not about questioning the player's toughness or ability, but about responsible long-term management.

"I think our job as coaches is [to] put our players in positions to have successful outcomes," McVay said . "He's as tough as it gets, just not feeling good enough. And I think it would be irresponsible on my part — and obviously talking with [team doctor] Reggie [Scott] — to ask him. He would do it and he could probably go be productive, but part of our job is to protect these tough dudes like him from themselves. … He's working as hard as he can to get himself feeling as good as possible. And we're hopeful and optimistic that good days are ahead," he added.

On the offensive side, the news is more encouraging. Wide receiver Puka Nacua is set to return after missing the previous two games with a hip injury. The issue first appeared during practice on September 17, when Nacua felt pain while trying to change direction. In the season opener he produced solid numbers with five receptions for 74 yards. So his return gives quarterback Matthew Stafford another reliable target and restores a key piece of the Rams' passing attack.

McVay was clearly encouraged by what he saw from Nacua in practice leading up to the game. He described the receiver's physical condition in positive terms while still noting the need for careful management of his snap count after the absence. "Physically he's getting in and out of his breaks, looks strong, looks sturdy, looks explosive," McVay said. "I think it'll really just be a feel for the overall conditioning. Hoping the magic of the jersey on Sundays, he's feeling real good there."

McVay also talked about what he felt seeing Nacua on pratice Thursday. "I thought he handled it well. In terms of the snap count, that's the thing that we have to be willing to navigate. But we've got confidence in some other guys that have played meaningful snaps in his absence. But he does look good. He looks strong, and he looks ready to go," McVay said.

The combination of Donald's absence and Nacua's return creates a mixed injury picture for the Rams heading into a significant NFC matchup. Donald's injury is a notable setback for a player who only recently returned to the field after coming out of retirement in late August. But having Puka Nacua is definitely a big relief.

articles.title: Group has 'exploded' after Wales win - Bellamy
articles.summary: Craig Bellamy says Wales' win over Norway has "thrown a hand grenade" into their Nations League group as they go in search of another victory against Denmark...
articles.body:
Craig Bellamy says Wales' win over Norway has "thrown a hand grenade" into their Nations League group as they go in search of another victory against Denmark in Cardiff on Sunday.

Wales remain bottom of Group A4 despite Thursday's morale-boosting triumph over the Norwegians, though they are level on points with Norway and Denmark at the halfway point in campaign.

They would take a significant step towards avoiding finishing last with another victory over the Danes, which would have a significant impact on their hopes of reaching the next European Championship.

If Wales end their Nations League campaign in third place or higher, they will be a top seed in the draw for Euro 2028 qualifying.

Bellamy says Portugal will win the group "unless a disaster happens" - but that the race for the places is wide open after his side shocked Norway.

"I don't know with the way the group's gone now because that [result] has thrown in a hand grenade," he said.

"Basically the group's exploded now between the three of us because obviously Denmark will look at it and say well they didn't expect that, so we all sit on three points apart from Portugal.

"Portugal have run away with this and they're going to win the group. Now can we really be in the mix with these two heavyweight Scandinavian teams? That's the aim. We'll see where that goes."

Wales came from behind against Norway to register their first win in Nations League A across two campaigns in the competition's top tier.

The victory also ended a six-match winless run stretching back to November 2025, with Bellamy admitting after the game that he had been through a "really difficult spell".

Wales will now attempt to build on what was the most notable success of the Bellamy era when they take on a Denmark side ranked 21st in the world.

"We have to perform like we did against Norway," Bellamy added.

"That's all I'm thinking about again - consistency and perform, perform, perform."

Nevertheless, Bellamy acknowledged that he is "definitely conscious" of the significance of finishing above fourth in the group.

"We see [the level when] we're playing against teams who are pot one, so if we don't have to play another pot one, then it's nice," he added.

"It's a real motivation of course. That would really help us."

Bellamy regularly makes significant changes to his side regardless of how results have gone.

Wales' options are limited in this window, with Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Dylan Lawlor and Harry Wilson all absent and David Brooks returning to his club after the opening defeat in Portugal.

Even so, Bellamy says he has no choice but to make alterations to the team which started against Norway as Wales play the final game in this new four-match international window.

"If I could pick the team that started the other night, [I would] all day," he said.

"[But it is] just not possible. Love it to make it possible, but it isn't. One or two didn't come through it. So not giving away the team of course, but there will be one or two changes because we have to."

Wales take on Denmark for the second time in seven days having been beaten in dispiriting fashion in the reverse fixture last weekend.

Bellamy said he "didn't recognise" his team in Copenhagen, adding: "I didn't recognise us. That's not what we do and how we've been when we've been at our best.

"We were too disconnected from front to back. We didn't create the overloads. It was too easy for [Denmark] to press us. Five men could press seven of our players - that's impossible.

"We learned a lot, I learned a lot from Denmark."

articles.title: Casey Jarvis holes out for eagle and builds a two-shot lead in the Dunhill Links
articles.summary: ANDREWS, Scotland (AP) — Casey Jarvis of South Africa holed out for eagle on his first hole and used the brilliant start to post a 7-under 65 on the Old Cour...
articles.body:
ST. ANDREWS, Scotland (AP) — Casey Jarvis of South Africa holed out for eagle on his first hole and used the brilliant start to post a 7-under 65 on the Old Course on Saturday, giving him a two-shot lead in the Dunhill Links Championship as he goes for his third European tour title of the year.

Jarvis played bogey-free on a breezy day at the home of golf, and didn't make a birdie putt longer than 6 feet in keeping his distance against the field.

Adrian Meronk of Poland, one of 22 players from LIV Golf in the field, birdied his opening four holes at Kingsbarns and had an eagle late in his round of 63. He was two shots behind with Matthew Jordan of England, who shot a 66 at Kingsbarns.

Thomas Detry of Belgium, another LIV player, was a further shot back after a 65 at St. Andrews.

Jarvis began his round on the 10th hole, and watched his wedge land about 6 feet beyond the hole and spin back into the cup. He followed that with a tee shot over the Strath bunker to 4 feet on the par-3 11th. When he two-putted for birdie on the 14th, he already was 5 under through five holes.

"I know I'm going to be feeling pressure tomorrow," said Jarvis, who won the Kenya Open and South African Open in consecutive weeks in February. "I have won twice this year. So I kind of know how to deal with it a little better. I still know I'm going to feel first tee nerves and pressure throughout the day."

Matt Fitzpatrick, coming off a victory last week in France, also got off to a great start with six birdies in his opening seven holes. He was even par the rest of the way — two birdies to go with two bogeys — for a 66 and wound up six shots behind, along with defending champion Robert MacIntyre (68).

Five-time major champion Brooks Koepka shot 70 on the Old Course and was eight back.

"Every golfer dreams of taking a lead, playing the Old Course on Sunday," Jarvis said. "I got goosebumps right now just standing here. I just can't wait for tomorrow. Even if I don't win, to be taking the lead, I'm just going to enjoy it as much as I can."

The cut was at 6-under 136. Tyrrell Hatton and Cam Smith, who won the British Open at St. Andrews in 2022, were among 14 players from LIV who missed the cut.

Meronk said he plans to play every week he can on the European tour with hopes of finishing high enough in the Race to Dubai to secure his card for 2027 and keep his options open depending on what happens with LIV.

"I've been playing really well the last couple of weeks. Just didn't get the full results," Meronk said. "Hopefully, this is the week. But just play my game tomorrow and see what happens at the end."

One 15-year-old male was arrested following spectator fights at the Oct. 2 football game between Buchtel and Firestone, according to the Akron Police Department.

Around 7:40 p.m. officers responded to Ellet's Joseph B. Yost Stadium after receiving reports of fights breaking out. Several units were needed to disperse the crowd of juveniles as multiple fights continued to start, according to Akron police Lt. Michael Murphy.

The teen was transported to the Summit County Juvenile Detention Center on charges of disorderly conduct, obstructing official business and resisting arrest. There were no reported injuries.

Officials canceled the remainder of the game because of fights involving spectators inside and outside of the stadium. Buchtel was ahead 20-0 and was declared the winner of the game .

When asked why the game was called off, Akron Public Schools Coordinator of Athletics Tom McKinnon said Friday night, "For the safety and security of everybody in the facility, it was deemed the best solution at this time was to call the game."

"There was a fight in the stands and then it just continued outside of the stadium," McKinnon said. "No players or coaches were involved."

articles.body:
Lorne Bickley continued his goalscoring form as he scored twice in Jersey Bulls 4-2 win over Ascot United at Springfield.

The win, which extended Jersey Bulls' unbeaten record in league to 25 matches, moved the islanders up to fourth in Isthmian League South Central.

Bickley fired in Bulls' opener after just five minutes after driving past his marker, but Ascot drew levels just two minutes later thanks to Fope Deru's strike.

But Bickley got on the end of James Sunley's pass to make it 2-1 after 14 minutes for his fifth goal in three games

Jack Lumsden headed in a Jay Giles cross to put the hosts 3-1 up after 20 minutes. while Casey Nixon missed a good chance to make it 4-1 in the 28th minute.

But Toby Ritzema made no mistake five minutes into the second half as he fired home from inside the box.

Chukwuka Uzor pulled a goal back for the visitors with 13 minutes left with a controlled finish from a chipped cross from the right.

"I thought going forward we were good at times, not as clinical as we could have been," Bulls manager Elliot Powell told BBC Radio Jersey.

"But we're disappointed to concede two again, they're not like us but they're becoming like us, three in a week, so we need to stamp it out.

"It was a really poor second goal that we conceded, so that's frustrating.

"I'm a glass half-empty type of guy anyway, so a 4-2 win's great but I'd much prefer a 2-0."

articles.title: Rutkowski earns Ballymena win at Solitude
articles.summary: Ballymena United make it back-to-back wins for the first time this season in the Irish Premiership with a hard-fought 1-0 win over Cliftonville at Solitude.
articles.body:
Ballymena United made it back-to-back wins for the first time this season in the Irish Premiership after a hard-fought 1-0 win over Cliftonville at Solitude.

Igor Rutkowski scored for the fourth game in succession as the Sky Blues followed up last week's win over Portadown.

Cliftonville played the entire second half with 10 men after teenage defender Paul Stanfield was sent off on his full Premiership debut for a second yellow card in first half injury time.

The result means Cliftonville have now lost four successive league games, three of them without scoring.

After a quiet opening half-hour, Cliftonville came within a whisker of taking the lead when Rhyss Campbell's low shot crashed off the inside of the post before being cleared.

Ballymena had few sights of goal but Cliftonville defender Kyle McClelland had to be sharp to block an Igor Rutkowski shot inside the penalty area.

The Reds had another opening when Brian Healy turned sharply in the box but with a clear sight of goal, Ballymena defender Kodi Lyons-Foster threw himself at the ball to divert the effort behind.

But just as Cliftonville were starting to get on top, they were dealt a blow in first half stoppage time when teenage defender Paul Stanfield was shown a second yellow card after catching Caoimhin McConnell with a high challenge.

Ballymena tried to make their numerical advantage count at the start of the second period with PJ Morrison making a sharp save to deny James Hood after a quickly taken short free kick by Finley Thorndike and then a minute later, the Scottish keeper did well to block a Thorndike effort.

But the visitors did go in front on 58 minutes when Caoimhin McConnell's shot was saved by Morrison but Rutkowski was first to react to smash home the loose ball.

Cliftonville spurned a glorious chance to level soon afterwards when substitute Liam McStravick won back possession just outside the Ballymena penalty area and bore down on goal but David Walsh stuck out a foot to make a vital stop.

There was late drama deep in stoppage time when Cliftonville striker Brian Healy collided with Ballymena keeper David Walsh as the pair chased a loose ball inside the penalty area but with the home side appealing for a penalty, referee Steven Gregg instead awarded a goal kick.
